text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them or vouches for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Shattuck expected to visit Belgrade and Pristina in the week from February 17 restoring U.S. high-level contacts with Yugoslav authorities interrupted over the local election crisis.
- Belgrade University deans and students to return to classes on February 24 if their remaining demands are met by that time.
- Yugoslav foreign ministry conveys dissatisfaction to the U.S. over participation of American congressmen, officially visiting the country, in opposition rallies.
- Some 4,000 striking teachers protest in front of Serbian government over unresolved problems in education, vow to continue protests.
- Textile and footwear producers are facing collapse due to halved export prices, high interests and non realistic dinar exchange rate.
- Serbian farmers' unions consider the government plan for payment of autumn crops to be unrealistic and do not expect it to be realised.
- New Kragujevac mayor calls citizens not to pay interest on outstanding bills because the government owes Kragujevac over 24 million dinars for social security.
POLITIKA
- Special law on local election results entered into effect Wednesday, electoral commissions have three days to determine election of councillors.
- Zastava cars of Kragujevac says it is negotiating with two potential partners and expects to make a decision on which one to chose in three months' time.
- Serbia's power company EPS managing board says there is sufficient power for all consumers, reappoints certain directors to other functions.
- Serbia preparing a new electoral law for electionof MP's, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minsiter Ratko Markovic.

- Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic considers that with the adoption of the special local election law a halt has been put to the local crisis and there is no more reason to protest in cities, says demonstrations had not been peaceful but threatening.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Out of 13 new Serbian ministers, seven are from the Yugoslav United Left (JUL), four from the ruling Socialist party of Serbia (SPS) and two are not from any party.
- Traditional two-day workers' gathering Red Banner will open in Kragujevac Friday organised by the official Yugoslav confederation of independent trade unions.
- Belgrade Bar Association decides to halt lawyers' strike but to continue other forms of protest until final reinstatement of local election results.
- Kosovo Albanian parties protest over OSCE's decision to appoint Max Van der Stoel as high commissioner for national minorities in Kosovo.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- New Yugoslav prime minister to be nominated by end of week, he will most probably again be the incumbent Radoje Kontic. The mandate of Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic expires in May and there is no possibility of re-election under the law.
-- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 43 05
